text: Solomon conscripted seventy thousand men as burden-bearers and eighty thousand to quarry stone in the hills, with three thousand six hundred to supervise them.
Then Solomon sent word to Huram king of Tyre: "Deal with me as you dealt with my father David, when you sent him cedar to build himself a house to live in.

I am about to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, to consecrate it to him for burning fragrant incense before him, for the regular setting out of the bread, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the appointed feasts of the LORD our God. This is an everlasting ordinance for Israel.
The house I am building will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.
Yet who is able to build him a house, when heaven and the highest heavens cannot contain him? And who am I to build him a house—except as a place to burn incense before him?

So send me a man skilled in working with gold and silver, bronze and iron, and with purple, crimson, and violet yarn, a man trained in engraving, to work with the skilled craftsmen I have here in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants are skilled at cutting the timber of Lebanon. My servants will work alongside yours
to provide me with timber in abundance, for the house I am building must be great and wonderful.

And for your servants, the woodsmen who cut the timber, I will supply twenty thousand kors of crushed wheat, twenty thousand kors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil."
Huram king of Tyre answered in a letter that he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them."

versions.text: Huram king of Tyre answered in a letter which he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them."
versions.explanation: The restrictive relative clause reads better with "that" than "which" in English, and it is smoother for oral reading.

versions.text: Huram king of Tyre answered in a letter that he sent to Solomon:
versions.explanation: The content of Huram's letter — בְּאַהֲבַת יְהוָה אֶת־עַמּוֹ נְתָנְךָ עֲלֵיהֶם מֶלֶךְ ("Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them") — was dropped in the previous revision. The change note only concerned "which" versus "that"; the loss of the quotation was unintentional and must be restored.

text: And Huram added: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth! He has given King David a wise son, endowed with insight and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
I am sending you Huram-abi, a skilled man of great understanding,

the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, his father a man of Tyre. He is trained to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, and in purple, violet, and crimson yarn and in fine linen. He is skilled in every kind of engraving and can carry out any design given to him. He will work with your craftsmen and with those of my lord David, your father.

versions.text: the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, his father a man of Tyre. He is trained to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, and in purple, violet, and crimson yarn and fine linen. He is skilled in every kind of engraving and can carry out any design given to him. He will work with your craftsmen and with those of my lord David, your father.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew lists purple, violet, fine linen, and crimson; the current wording attaches "yarn" to crimson and appends "fine linen" awkwardly at the end of the phrase, which also blurs that fine linen is a fabric rather than a dyed yarn. Adding "and in" before "fine linen" separates the categories and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: Now then, let my lord send his servants the wheat and barley, the oil and wine that he spoke of.

versions.text: Now then, let my lord send his servants the wheat and barley, the oil and wine that he promised.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew אָמַר means "spoke of / mentioned"; "promised" adds a nuance of commitment not present in the text, since Solomon had offered these goods rather than promising them in a covenantal sense.

text: We will cut all the timber from Lebanon that you need and float it in rafts by sea to Joppa, and you can haul it up to Jerusalem."
Solomon took a census of all the foreigners residing in the land of Israel, following the census his father David had taken, and they numbered a hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
He assigned seventy thousand of them as burden-bearers, eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hills, and three thousand six hundred as foremen to keep the people at work.
